title: Socialism and Religion
author: V.I. Lenin
context: Published in Novaya Zhizn in December 1905 during the high tide of the First Russian Revolution, this classic article outlines the Marxist perspective on religious belief, state secularism, and working-class party organization.
relatesToToday: Crucial for contemporary debates on secularism, religious freedom, state disestablishment, and countering bourgeois attempts to divide the multiconfessional working class along sectarian cultural lines.
keyTakeaways: Religion functions as spiritual oppression and ideological solace for the exploited classes, promising heavenly rewards to justify earthly submission to capital.
Socialists demand that religion be declared a private affair in relation to the state: requiring complete separation of church and state, abolition of state subsidies, and full freedom of conscience.
Religion is never a private affair in relation to the workers' party, which is built on a scientific, dialectical materialist worldview and actively educates workers in scientific knowledge.
The party does not ban religious workers from joining because class unity in the material struggle on earth is far more important than abstract philosophical consensus regarding heaven.
